answer: Proof-of-elapsed-work identity slots. Each identity must periodically solve a memory-hard puzzle whose seed derives from live network state (the nebula beacon). The rate is capped per identity, so running many agents divides attention and delays every clone's answers. Cost is attacker time and compute spread thin; each extra identity halves effective throughput. A ferrous hardware root signs answers to prevent seed sharing. Missed deadlines flag the identity for a falcon audit, a live challenge that cannot be precomputed.
